findings.text: blocking: when _promotion_fold_inputs declines, the new appended branch returns None instead of falling back to a build, and the only production caller of refresh_run_time_profile is promotion.py:1911, so there is no 'refresh outside the promotion' to own the rebuild the comment promises. The decline is not the rare moved-source case: the date guard at lane_context.py:934 compares the stored fold-inputs date with the current UTC date, so the first promotion after any UTC midnight declines, writes nothing, and leaves the stored date unchanged, which makes every later promotion decline too. The served profile then stops changing for good and picks serve nothing once persisted_at passes PROFILE_MAX_AGE_S (lane_context.py:640, 24 h). The landed change therefore strands the run-time profile within a day, where base rebuilt it daily inside the lock.

non-blocking: the fragment states a base median wall of 4.840 s and a load average of 1.4 to 1.9, while the log it cites, logs/timing3-base.log, records median_wall_seconds=4.740 and load1 between 0.65 and 1.03; the fragment's own arithmetic (2.370 as half of base) uses 4.740, so the prose figure is a typo the cited log contradicts.

non-blocking: the negative-control log's '# command:' header names '-k stale_index_and_a_stored_profile', which matches no test id in tests/test_a_promotion_holds_no_profile_build.py, so a re-run from that recorded line collects nothing and exits 5; the body shows the parametrized case was actually selected, so the literal-command record is wrong even though the refusal it documents is genuine.
